title: Procedure for Decellularization of Porcine Heart by Retrograde Coronary Perfusion
protocol: Harvest porcine organ immediately after euthanasia.
Rinse off excess blood from the harvested tissue.
Trim heart of excess fat and tissue, keeping atria and aorta intact.
Separate pulmonary artery from the aorta by trimming away fat.
Discard any tissue with cuts appropriately.
Wrap each heart individually in freezer paper.
Store all tissue in a -80°C freezer for at least 24 hours.
Thaw one intact frozen porcine heart in Type 1 water overnight at 4°C.
Pat the heart dry after thawing completely.
Weigh the heart and record its weight.
Connect size 18 Masterflex tubing to the ¼" end of a barbed reducer.
Insert barbed reducer and tubing inside the aorta.
Place 2 hose clamps or secure zip ties around the aorta, just below the brachiocephalic trunk.
Use a 30 or 60 ml syringe to fill the tubing with Type I water.
Insert the tubing within the cartridge of a Masterflex roller pump at its midpoint.
Submerge the inflow end of the tubing in the bottom of a 4 L beaker filled with 2.5 L of water and secure the tubing.
Place the heart in the beaker filled with water.
Prime the pump to remove air bubbles.
If bubbles are observed coming from the aorta, reposition or secure the aorta with additional ties.
Place the 4 L beaker containing 3 L of a 0.2% Trypsin/0.05% EDTA/0.05% NaN3 solution on a stir plate and warm it to 37 °C.
Set the pump to a flow rate of 400 ml/min, ensuring that the correct tubing size is selected.
Flush the heart with Type I water for 15-25 min.
Substitute fresh solution every 5-10 min or as needed based on the amount of blood removed from the heart.
Stop the pump and transfer the heart to a separate beaker filled with 2X Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS).
Start the pump and increase the flow rate to 700 ml/min.
Change the PBS solution every 5 min for 15 min.
Transfer the heart to Type I water for 10 min.
Increase the flow rate to 750 ml/min in Type I water.
Transfer the heart to a beaker containing 0.2% Trypsin/0.05% EDTA/0.05% NaN3 at 37 °C.
Start the pump and increase the flow rate to 1,200 ml/min.
Increase the pump speed to 1,500 ml/min after 1 hour.
Increase the pump speed to 1,800 ml/min after an additional hour.
Perfuse the tissue with water for 10 min after each solution perfusion.
Rinse the tissue in 2X PBS for 10 min at room temperature.
Remove solution from the original beaker.
Add rinse solutions and circulate within the beaker containing submerged heart.
Perfuse water at 1,900 ml/min after Trypsin/EDTA/NaN3 solution.
Perfuse 2X PBS at 1950 ml/min following water perfusion.
Transfer heart to a solution of 3% Triton X-100/0.05% EDTA/0.05% NaN3 at room temperature.
Increase pump speed to 2,000 ml/min and perfuse for one hour.
Remove the 3% Triton X-100/0.05% EDTA/0.05% NaN3 solution from beaker.
Replace with fresh solution and increase pump speed to 2100 ml/min.
Perfuse fresh solution at 2100 ml/min for an additional hour and a half.
Rinse tissue in Type I water at 2150 ml/min for 10 min after perfusion.
Rinse the tissue in 2X PBS at 2180 ml/min for 10 min at room temperature.
Transfer heart to a 4% Sodium Deoxycholate solution at room temperature.
Increase pump speed to 2,200 ml/min and perfuse the solution for 3 hr.
Rinse the tissue in Type I water at 2,200 ml/min for 15 min.
Change the solution after 5-10 min.
Rinse the tissue in 2X PBS at 2,200 ml/min for 15 min.
Change the solution after 5-10 min.
Perform a 5 min rinse with Type I water at 750 ml/min.
Perform a 5 min rinse with 1X PBS at 1,500 ml/min.
Transfer the heart to a 0.1% peracetic acid/4% ethanol solution.
Perfuse the solution for 1.5 hr at 2,200 ml/min.
Perfuse the tissue with 1X PBS for 15 min.
Wash the tissue in Type I water twice for 5 min each.
Repeat the series of rinses once more.
Turn off the pump and remove the heart from solution to drain.
Cut ties from the aorta and remove all tubing.
Place the heart in an empty beaker to drain for 1 hr.
Drain excess liquid periodically.
Lay the heart on an absorbent pad to fully drain.
Record the weight of the cardiac extracellular matrix (C-ECM).
Dissect the right and left ventricles, as well as the ventricular septum for DNA quantification and histological processing.
Freeze the C-ECM at -80 °C for at least 2 hr before lyophilization.
